📊 A single line in the ONS bulletin that deserved a lot more attention:

UK inflation in August was 3.1%.
France: 2.7%.
Germany: 2.9%.

Same disrupted global energy market. Same war. Same month. Three different results. 🇬🇧🇫🇷🇩🇪

Every time prices rise we're told it's "global headwinds" — events beyond anyone's control. But if the shock is global and shared, it can't explain why we're coming in above our neighbours.

Let me be fair: a real chunk of August's rise WAS imported. Core inflation didn't move at all — it was transport and fuel doing the damage. I'm not going to pretend otherwise.

But that's exactly what makes the comparison so awkward. If the shock is shared, the gap is ours. 🤷

You can't claim credit for the good numbers and blame the planet for the bad ones.

And the Budget lands on 28 October, with tax rises not ruled out. 📉

Full piece 👉 https://lukeparker.co.uk/articles/uk-inflation-higher-than-france-germany-september-2026.html
